title: Adding and subtracting coplanar vectors mark scheme

questions.answer: A vector quantity is a physical quantity that has magnitude and direction. A complete numerical report gives its magnitude, an appropriate unit and its direction.
accepted_alternatives: A quantity with size and a specified direction, reported with its value, unit and direction.
questions.unit_policy: No particular numerical unit is required, but an appropriate unit must be named as part of a complete vector report.
questions.tolerance: Both the controlled definition and the complete-report requirement are needed for full marks.

marking_points.text: States that a vector quantity is a physical quantity that has magnitude and direction
States that a complete numerical vector report includes magnitude, an appropriate unit and direction

questions.unit_policy: No unit is required for a selected option.

option_feedback.A: Correct. The second vector begins at the first vector's head, and the resultant joins the original start to the final point.
option_feedback.B: The arrow between two heads represents a difference when the given vectors share a tail, not their sum.
option_feedback.C: Reversing B constructs A minus B, not A plus B.
option_feedback.D: Magnitudes can be added directly only when the vectors point along the same line in the same direction.

marking_points.text: Selects A as the correct head-to-tail construction for vector addition

questions.unit_policy: The selected option includes the required unit N and direction east.

option_feedback.A: The magnitudes would add to 23 N only if both forces pointed east.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The opposite vectors partly cancel, giving 14 minus 9 = 5 N in the direction of the larger eastward force.
option_feedback.C: The magnitude is 5 N, but the larger vector points east rather than west.
option_feedback.D: Both the direct addition of magnitudes and the westward direction are incorrect.

marking_points.text: Selects B, giving a resultant of 5 N east

questions.unit_policy: No unit is required for a selected operation.

option_feedback.A: A minus B requires B, not A, to be reversed.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Subtracting B is equivalent to adding the reversed vector minus B to A.
option_feedback.C: Subtraction changes the direction of B, so its direction cannot be ignored.
option_feedback.D: Placing heads together and adding magnitudes does not construct vector subtraction.

marking_points.text: Selects B, reversing vector B and adding the reversed vector to A head-to-tail

questions.answer: The vectors form a right-angled head-to-tail triangle. The resultant is 13 km at 22.6 degrees north of east.
accepted_alternatives: 13.0 km at 23 degrees north of east
questions.unit_policy: km is required for magnitude and a degree value with north of east is required for direction.
questions.tolerance: Accept 13 km exactly or 13.0 km, and an angle from 22.5 to 22.7 degrees north of east.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A 12-square arrow is drawn east from the start, followed by a 5-square arrow north from its head. R is drawn and labelled from the original start to the final point.
accepted_alternatives: An equivalent correctly scaled head-to-tail diagram using a separately stated scale
parts.unit_policy: The supplied scale is 1 square per km.
parts.tolerance: Allow normal drawing tolerance while preserving scale, direction and connectivity.

marking_points.text: Draws the 12 km east and 5.0 km north vectors to scale in a correct head-to-tail chain
Draws and labels R from the original start to the final point with the correct arrow direction

parts.label: (b)
parts.tolerance: Accept 13 km or 13.0 km from a valid right-triangle calculation.

marking_points.text: Uses the right-angled vector triangle to obtain a resultant magnitude of 13 km

parts.label: (c)
parts.unit_policy: A degree value and the direction north of east are required.
parts.tolerance: Accept 22.5 to 22.7 degrees north of east, or 23 degrees north of east if rounded to two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Uses $\tan\theta=5.0/12$ for an angle measured north of east
Obtains a direction of $22.6^\circ$ north of east

questions.answer: Reverse B to make 3.0 m south, then add it head-to-tail to A. The resultant is 7.62 m at 23.2 degrees south of east.
accepted_alternatives: 7.6 m at 23 degrees south of east
questions.unit_policy: m is required for magnitude and a degree value with south of east is required for direction.
questions.tolerance: Accept magnitude 7.61 to 7.63 m and direction 23.1 to 23.3 degrees south of east.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: B is reversed to a 3.0 m south vector and placed at the head of A. R is drawn from A's tail to the final head, pointing south of east.
accepted_alternatives: An equivalent correctly oriented head-to-tail construction
parts.unit_policy: Lengths must preserve the stated vector magnitudes on one consistent diagram scale.

marking_points.text: Reverses B to a 3.0 m south vector and places it head-to-tail after A
Draws and labels R from the original tail of A to the final head, directed south of east

parts.label: (b)
parts.tolerance: Accept 7.61 to 7.63 m, or 7.6 m to two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Forms $R=\sqrt{7.0^2+3.0^2}$ from the completed right-angled vector triangle
Obtains a resultant magnitude of 7.62 m

parts.label: (c)
parts.unit_policy: A degree value and the direction south of east are required.
parts.tolerance: Accept 23.1 to 23.3 degrees south of east, or 23 degrees south of east to two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Uses $\tan\theta=3.0/7.0$ for an angle measured from east
Obtains a direction of $23.2^\circ$ south of east

questions.answer: Time is scalar and each displacement is vector. The head-to-tail route ends 5.0 m west and 12 m south of the start, giving a resultant of 13 m at 67.4 degrees south of west.
accepted_alternatives: 13.0 m at 22.6 degrees west of south
questions.unit_policy: The final magnitude requires m and the direction requires a degree value with an unambiguous compass description.
questions.tolerance: Accept an equivalent compass bearing or angle description derived from the same southwest resultant.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Time is scalar because it has magnitude only. Each displacement is vector because it has magnitude and direction.
accepted_alternatives: Duration is scalar; all three directed movements are vectors.
parts.unit_policy: No new numerical unit is required.
parts.tolerance: All four quantities must be classified with the defining distinction for full marks.

marking_points.text: Classifies time as a scalar quantity because it has magnitude only
Classifies all three displacements as vector quantities because each has magnitude and direction

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The route is drawn 9 squares west, then 12 squares south, then 4 squares east. R is drawn from the start to the final point and labelled.
accepted_alternatives: An equivalent correctly scaled head-to-tail route using a separately stated scale
parts.unit_policy: The supplied scale is 1 square per m.
parts.tolerance: Allow normal drawing tolerance while preserving the three directions and connectivity.

marking_points.text: Draws the 9.0 m west, 12 m south and 4.0 m east vectors to scale in one continuous head-to-tail chain
Draws and labels R from the original start to the final point with the correct southwest direction

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The horizontal vectors combine to 5.0 m west. Hence $R=\sqrt{5.0^2+12^2}=13$ m. With $\tan\theta=12/5.0$, $\theta=67.4^\circ$ south of west.
accepted_alternatives: 13.0 m at 22.6 degrees west of south
parts.unit_policy: m is required for magnitude and an unambiguous degree direction is required.
parts.tolerance: Accept 13 m exactly and 67.3 to 67.5 degrees south of west, or the complementary direction 22.5 to 22.7 degrees west of south.

marking_points.text: Combines the opposing horizontal displacements to obtain 5.0 m west while retaining 12 m south
Forms $R=\sqrt{5.0^2+12^2}$ from the final right-angled vector triangle
Obtains a resultant magnitude of 13 m
Obtains a direction of $67.4^\circ$ south of west or an equivalent unambiguous direction
